title: Final Boss: The Order Desk
summary: Four challenges that pull the whole track together: generics, reflection, events, injection and concurrency.

steps.title: The last four
body: You are building the back end of a small shop, one piece at a time. Each challenge is a part you would find in a real code base:
1. a generic **repository** that stores things and reports problems with `Result<T>`
2. an **attribute-driven validator** that checks any object
3. an **event-driven order processor** with injected dependencies
4. an **async job runner** with bounded concurrency and cancellation
Nothing here is new. Everything here is combined. Read each task fully before you type, and use the hints if you get stuck: that is what they are for.

steps.title: 1. A generic repository
prompt: Complete `Repository<T>`, an in-memory store for anything that has an `Id`. `IEntity` and `Result<T>` are given.
- Constrain `T` so that it must be a class that implements `IEntity`.
- `Result<T> Add(T item)` stores the item and returns `Success(item)`. If an item with that `Id` is already stored, it stores nothing and returns `Fail("Duplicate id 7")` (with the real id).
- `Result<T> Get(int id)` returns `Success(item)`, or `Fail("Not found: 7")`.
- `IEnumerable<T> Query(Func<T, bool> predicate)` returns the matching items **ordered by `Id`**.
- `int Count` is the number of stored items.
The tests use `record Book(int Id, string Title, int Year) : IEntity;`.
starter: record Result<T>(bool Ok, T? Value, string Error)
public static Result<T> Success(T value) => new(true, value, "");
public static Result<T> Fail(string error) => new(false, default, error);
public IEnumerable<T> Query(Func<T, bool> predicate) => Enumerable.Empty<T>();
solution: record Result<T>(bool Ok, T? Value, string Error)
public static Result<T> Success(T value) => new(true, value, "");
public static Result<T> Fail(string error) => new(false, default, error);
class Repository<T> where T : class, IEntity
_items.TryGetValue(id, out T? item) ? Result<T>.Success(item) : Result<T>.Fail($"Not found: {id}");
template: var repo = new Repository<Book>();
var dune = new Book(2, "Dune", 1965);
var added = repo.Add(dune);
Dojo.Check("Add returns Ok with the item for a new id", added.Ok && ReferenceEquals(added.Value, dune));
repo.Add(new Book(3, "Neuromancer", 1984));
repo.Add(new Book(1, "Emma", 1815));
var dup = repo.Add(new Book(2, "Impostor", 2000));
Dojo.Check("Adding a second item with id 2 is not Ok", !dup.Ok);
Dojo.Eq("Its error is \"Duplicate id 2\"", "Duplicate id 2", dup.Error);
Dojo.Eq("Count is 3 after three good adds and one duplicate", 3, repo.Count);
var found = repo.Get(2);
Dojo.Check("Get(2) is Ok and still returns the original Dune", found.Ok && ReferenceEquals(found.Value, dune));
var missing = repo.Get(9);
Dojo.Check("Get(9) is not Ok and has no Value", !missing.Ok && missing.Value == null);
Dojo.Eq("Its error is \"Not found: 9\"", "Not found: 9", missing.Error);
Dojo.Eq("Query(b => b.Year < 1970) returns Emma, Dune (ordered by Id)", "Emma, Dune", string.Join(", ", repo.Query(b => b.Year < 1970).Select(b => b.Title)));
Dojo.Eq("Query(b => true) returns everything ordered by Id", "Emma, Dune, Neuromancer", string.Join(", ", repo.Query(b => true).Select(b => b.Title)));
Dojo.Eq("Query with no match is empty", 0, repo.Query(b => b.Year > 2020).Count());
Dojo.Check("T is constrained to IEntity", typeof(Repository<>).GetGenericArguments()[0].GetGenericParameterConstraints().Contains(typeof(IEntity)), "Add `where T : class, IEntity`.");
record Book(int Id, string Title, int Year) : IEntity;
{{CODE}}
hints: `class Repository<T> where T : class, IEntity`. The constraint is what lets you write `item.Id`.
Keep the items in a `Dictionary<int, T>` keyed by id. `ContainsKey` answers the duplicate question, `TryGetValue` answers `Get`.

steps.title: 2. Rules as attributes
prompt: Build a validator where **each attribute carries its own rule**. The base class `RuleAttribute` and `Result<T>` are given.
**`[MinLength(n)]`**: `Check` returns `null` when the value is a string of at least `n` characters. Otherwise (shorter, or `null`) it returns `"{name} must be at least {n} characters"`.
**`[Positive]`**: `Check` returns `null` when the value is an `int` greater than 0. Otherwise it returns `"{name} must be positive"`.
**`Validator.Validate<T>(T item)`**:
- visits the public properties of `T` **in order of property name**
- for every `RuleAttribute` on a property, calls `Check(propertyName, value)`
- with no errors, returns `Result<T>.Success(item)`
- otherwise returns `Result<T>.Fail(...)` with all the error messages joined by `"; "`
For a class with `[MinLength(3)] Guest` and `[Positive] Seats`, a guest of `"Al"` with 0 seats fails with `Guest must be at least 3 characters; Seats must be positive`.
`Validate` must not know about `MinLength` or `Positive`: it only talks to `RuleAttribute`. `using System.Reflection;` is already in place.
starter: record Result<T>(bool Ok, T? Value, string Error)
public static Result<T> Success(T value) => new(true, value, "");
public static Result<T> Fail(string error) => new(false, default, error);
// Returns an error message, or null when the value is fine.
public abstract string? Check(string name, object? value);
public override string? Check(string name, object? value) => null;   // TODO
public override string? Check(string name, object? value) => null;   // TODO
public static Result<T> Validate<T>(T item) where T : class
// TODO: collect the errors from every rule on every property
solution: record Result<T>(bool Ok, T? Value, string Error)
public static Result<T> Success(T value) => new(true, value, "");
public static Result<T> Fail(string error) => new(false, default, error);
// Returns an error message, or null when the value is fine.
public abstract string? Check(string name, object? value);
public override string? Check(string name, object? value) =>
value is string text && text.Length >= _length ? null : $"{name} must be at least {_length} characters";
public override string? Check(string name, object? value) =>
value is int number && number > 0 ? null : $"{name} must be positive";
public static Result<T> Validate<T>(T item) where T : class
template: using System.Reflection;
Dojo.Eq("[MinLength(2)] accepts \"ab\"", null, new MinLengthAttribute(2).Check("Tag", "ab"));
Dojo.Eq("[MinLength(2)] rejects \"a\"", "Tag must be at least 2 characters", new MinLengthAttribute(2).Check("Tag", "a"));
Dojo.Eq("[MinLength(2)] rejects null", "Tag must be at least 2 characters", new MinLengthAttribute(2).Check("Tag", null));
Dojo.Eq("[Positive] accepts 1", null, new PositiveAttribute().Check("Qty", 1));
Dojo.Eq("[Positive] rejects 0", "Qty must be positive", new PositiveAttribute().Check("Qty", 0));
var good = new Booking { Guest = "Ana", Seats = 2 };
var r1 = Validator.Validate(good);
Dojo.Check("A valid booking is Ok and carries the same object", r1.Ok && ReferenceEquals(r1.Value, good));
var r2 = Validator.Validate(new Booking { Guest = "Al", Seats = 2 });
Dojo.Check("A booking for \"Al\" is not Ok", !r2.Ok);
Dojo.Eq("Its error names the Guest rule", "Guest must be at least 3 characters", r2.Error);
var r3 = Validator.Validate(new Booking { Guest = "Ben", Seats = 0 });
Dojo.Eq("A booking for 0 seats", "Seats must be positive", r3.Error);
var r4 = Validator.Validate(new Booking { Guest = null, Seats = -1 });
Dojo.Eq("Two problems are joined with \"; \" in property-name order", "Guest must be at least 3 characters; Seats must be positive", r4.Error);
var r5 = Validator.Validate(new Coupon { Percent = 10, Code = "SAVE" });
Dojo.Eq("It works for a different class: Coupon", "Code must be at least 5 characters", r5.Error);
var r6 = Validator.Validate(new Coupon { Percent = 0, Code = "X" });
Dojo.Eq("Coupon errors come in property-name order too", "Code must be at least 5 characters; Percent must be positive", r6.Error);
class Booking
[MinLength(3)] public string? Guest { get; set; }
public string? Note { get; set; }
[Positive] public int Seats { get; set; }
class Coupon
[Positive] public int Percent { get; set; }
[MinLength(5)] public string? Code { get; set; }
{{CODE}}

forbid.message: Validate only asks for RuleAttribute, never for a specific rule

hints: Do the two attributes first. Pattern matching keeps them short: `value is string text && text.Length >= _length ? null : $"..."`.

In `Validate`: `foreach (PropertyInfo prop in typeof(T).GetProperties().OrderBy(p => p.Name))`, read `prop.GetValue(item)`, then loop over `prop.GetCustomAttributes<RuleAttribute>()`. Asking for the base class returns every derived rule.
Collect non-null results of `rule.Check(prop.Name, value)` in a list. At the end: `errors.Count == 0 ? Result<T>.Success(item) : Result<T>.Fail(string.Join("; ", errors))`.

steps.title: 3. An event-driven order processor
prompt: Two classes, wired together with injection and events. The records and interfaces are given.
**`OrderProcessor`**
- receives an `IPaymentGateway` through its constructor
- has two events of type `EventHandler<Order>`: `OrderPaid` and `OrderRejected`
- `Result<Order> Process(Order order)`:
- a `Total` of zero or less returns `Fail("Invalid total")`. The gateway is **not** called and no event is raised.
- otherwise it calls `Charge(order.Customer, order.Total)`. If that returns `false`, it raises `OrderRejected` and returns `Fail("Payment declined")`.
- if the charge succeeds, it raises `OrderPaid` and returns `Success(order)`.
- events are raised with the processor as sender, and must be safe with no subscribers
**`ReceiptMailer`**
- receives an `IEmailSender` through its constructor
- `Subscribe(OrderProcessor processor)` starts listening to `OrderPaid`. For each paid order it calls `Send(order.Customer, "Receipt for order 7")` (with the real id).
- `Unsubscribe(OrderProcessor processor)` stops listening. After that, no more emails.
starter: record Order(int Id, string Customer, decimal Total);
record Result<T>(bool Ok, T? Value, string Error)
public static Result<T> Success(T value) => new(true, value, "");
public static Result<T> Fail(string error) => new(false, default, error);
interface IPaymentGateway { bool Charge(string customer, decimal amount); }
interface IEmailSender { void Send(string to, string subject); }
// TODO: declare the events OrderPaid and OrderRejected
solution: record Order(int Id, string Customer, decimal Total);
record Result<T>(bool Ok, T? Value, string Error)
public static Result<T> Success(T value) => new(true, value, "");
public static Result<T> Fail(string error) => new(false, default, error);
interface IPaymentGateway { bool Charge(string customer, decimal amount); }
interface IEmailSender { void Send(string to, string subject); }
private void OnOrderPaid(object? sender, Order order) =>
template: var gateway = new FakeGateway(100m);
var outbox = new FakeEmailSender();
var processor = new OrderProcessor(gateway);
Dojo.Try("Processing with no subscribers works and returns Ok", () =>
var first = processor.Process(new Order(1, "ana@example.com", 40m));
Dojo.Check("Processing with no subscribers works and returns Ok", first.Ok);
var paid = new List<int>();
var rejected = new List<int>();
object? who = null;
processor.OrderPaid += (s, o) => { paid.Add(o.Id); who = s; };
processor.OrderRejected += (s, o) => rejected.Add(o.Id);
var mailer = new ReceiptMailer(outbox);
mailer.Subscribe(processor);
var ok = processor.Process(new Order(2, "ben@example.com", 60m));
Dojo.Check("A paid order returns Ok and carries the order", ok.Ok && ok.Value?.Id == 2);
var declined = processor.Process(new Order(3, "cy@example.com", 500m));
Dojo.Check("A declined order is not Ok", !declined.Ok);
Dojo.Eq("Its error is \"Payment declined\"", "Payment declined", declined.Error);
int chargesBefore = gateway.Charges.Count;
var invalid = processor.Process(new Order(4, "di@example.com", 0m));
Dojo.Eq("A total of 0 fails with \"Invalid total\"", "Invalid total", invalid.Error);
Dojo.Eq("An invalid order never reaches the gateway", chargesBefore, gateway.Charges.Count);
Dojo.Eq("The gateway was charged with customer and total", "ben@example.com 60", gateway.Charges.Count > 1 ? gateway.Charges[1] : "(no charge)");
Dojo.Eq("OrderPaid was raised for order 2 only", "2", string.Join(",", paid));
Dojo.Eq("OrderRejected was raised for order 3 only", "3", string.Join(",", rejected));
Dojo.Check("The sender of the event is the processor", ReferenceEquals(who, processor));
Dojo.Eq("The mailer sent exactly one receipt", "ben@example.com: Receipt for order 2", string.Join(" | ", outbox.Sent));
mailer.Unsubscribe(processor);
processor.Process(new Order(5, "eve@example.com", 10m));
Dojo.Eq("After Unsubscribe the mailer sends nothing more", 1, outbox.Sent.Count);
Dojo.Eq("Other subscribers still hear about order 5", "2,5", string.Join(",", paid));
Dojo.Check("OrderPaid and OrderRejected are declared with the event keyword", typeof(OrderProcessor).GetEvent("OrderPaid") != null && typeof(OrderProcessor).GetEvent("OrderRejected") != null);
class FakeGateway : IPaymentGateway
private readonly decimal _limit;
public FakeGateway(decimal limit) => _limit = limit;
public List<string> Charges { get; } = new();
public bool Charge(string customer, decimal amount)
Charges.Add($"{customer} {amount}");
return amount <= _limit;
class FakeEmailSender : IEmailSender
public List<string> Sent { get; } = new();
public void Send(string to, string subject) => Sent.Add($"{to}: {subject}");
{{CODE}}
hints: Declare the events as `public event EventHandler<Order>? OrderPaid;` and raise them with `OrderPaid?.Invoke(this, order);`.
In `Process`, check the total first and return early. Only then call the gateway, so an invalid order never reaches it.

`Unsubscribe` only works if `Subscribe` used a named method: `private void OnOrderPaid(object? sender, Order order) => _sender.Send(...)`, then `processor.OrderPaid += OnOrderPaid;` and `-= OnOrderPaid;`.

steps.title: 4. sk sync, a bounded job runner
prompt: The last one, and it goes straight into your Sidekick: **`sk sync`** saves your data, writes a backup and exports your timesheet, two jobs at a time, and reports each one.
Write the records and the class:
```csharp
record Job(string Name, Func<CancellationToken, Task> Run);
record JobResult(string Name, bool Ok, string Message);
`class JobRunner`:
- Constructor `JobRunner(int maxParallel)`; below 1 throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`.

- `async Task<List<JobResult>> RunAsync(IEnumerable<Job> jobs, CancellationToken cancel = default)`: run every job, never more than `maxParallel` at once, passing `cancel` to each. Return one result per job **in the order given**:
- finished: `JobResult(name, true, "ok")`
- threw: `JobResult(name, false, exception.Message)`; the other jobs keep going
- cancelled (while running, or while waiting for a slot): `JobResult(name, false, "cancelled")`. A job still waiting for a slot when `cancel` fires must never start.
`RunAsync` itself does not throw for failed or cancelled jobs: the report says what happened. The tests cancel after 20 ms while jobs would take 2 s each.
starter: record Job(string Name, Func<CancellationToken, Task> Run);
record JobResult(string Name, bool Ok, string Message);
public async Task<List<JobResult>> RunAsync(IEnumerable<Job> jobs, CancellationToken cancel = default)
solution: record Job(string Name, Func<CancellationToken, Task> Run);
record JobResult(string Name, bool Ok, string Message);
if (maxParallel < 1) throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(maxParallel), "Run at least one job at a time.");
public async Task<List<JobResult>> RunAsync(IEnumerable<Job> jobs, CancellationToken cancel = default)
template: int dojoIn = 0, dojoMax = 0;
var dojoGate = new object();
Job DojoJob(string name, int ms) => new(name, async ct =>
lock (dojoGate) { dojoIn++; dojoMax = Math.Max(dojoMax, dojoIn); }
try { await Task.Delay(ms, ct); }
finally { lock (dojoGate) dojoIn--; }
var dojoResults = await new JobRunner(2).RunAsync(Enumerable.Range(1, 5).Select(i => DojoJob($"job{i}", 20)).ToList());
Dojo.Eq("every job reports ok, in the order given",
new List<JobResult> { new("job1", true, "ok"), new("job2", true, "ok"), new("job3", true, "ok"), new("job4", true, "ok"), new("job5", true, "ok") }, dojoResults);
Dojo.Eq("never more than 2 at once, and both slots are used", 2, dojoMax);
var dojoMixed = await new JobRunner(3).RunAsync(new List<Job>
DojoJob("save", 5),
new("backup", async ct => { await Task.Delay(5, ct); throw new IOException("disk full"); }),
DojoJob("timesheet", 5),
Dojo.Eq("a failing job reports its message and the others still run",
new List<JobResult> { new("save", true, "ok"), new("backup", false, "disk full"), new("timesheet", true, "ok") }, dojoMixed);
int dojoStarted = 0;
using var dojoCts = new CancellationTokenSource(20);
var dojoSlow = Enumerable.Range(1, 4).Select(i => new Job($"slow{i}", async ct => { Interlocked.Increment(ref dojoStarted); await Task.Delay(2000, ct); })).ToList();
var dojoCancelled = await new JobRunner(2).RunAsync(dojoSlow, dojoCts.Token);
Dojo.Eq("after cancelling, every job reports cancelled",
new List<string> { "slow1 cancelled", "slow2 cancelled", "slow3 cancelled", "slow4 cancelled" },
dojoCancelled.Select(r => $"{r.Name} {(r.Ok ? "ok" : r.Message)}").ToList());
Dojo.Check("jobs waiting for a slot never start once cancelled", dojoStarted <= 2, $"{dojoStarted} jobs started");
Dojo.Eq("no jobs, no results", 0, (await new JobRunner(1).RunAsync(new List<Job>())).Count);
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentOutOfRangeException>("maxParallel must be at least 1", () => new JobRunner(0));
{{CODE}}

require.message: Limits parallel jobs with a SemaphoreSlim
Waits for all jobs with Task.WhenAll

hints: Start one task per job with `jobs.Select(async job => { ... }).ToList()` and `await Task.WhenAll(...)`: that keeps the order.
Wait for a slot with `await gate.WaitAsync(cancel)` in its own `try`: if that throws `OperationCanceledException` the job never got a slot, so return `cancelled` without releasing.

Around `await job.Run(cancel)`: `catch (OperationCanceledException) when (cancel.IsCancellationRequested)` gives `cancelled`, `catch (Exception e)` gives `e.Message`, and `finally { gate.Release(); }`.
steps.explain: Run `sk sync` in your Sidekick's Code space: three jobs, two at a time, one line each. Your ForEachLimited from the Async boss had the same shape; this one adds cancellation and a report instead of an exception.
